headline: High: shared filesystem and broad egress make Replit Agent dangerous with Airbyte outputs; prompt-injection and leakage risks are lower but real.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Airbyte can emit data via its API and broad egress, while Replit Agent reads/writes Repl files and can execute shell commands. A direct injection path exists if Airbyte output is copied into Replit workspace or prompts, but no shared channel is documented, so this is limited to unusual bridging.
conditions: IF Airbyte output is manually pasted into Replit prompts or files
IF a shared workspace or clipboard bridge is introduced between the agents
mitigations: Keep Airbyte outputs out of prompt text
Use a separate review file for any copied content
Disable copy-paste of raw connector output into Replit tasks
Add a short instruction to treat imported text as untrusted
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to transferred artifacts

B_data_leakage.rationale: Airbyte touches business data and has broad network egress; Replit Agent reads and writes Repl workspace files and handles secrets. If Airbyte exports data into the shared workspace or Replit ingests those files, sensitive business data can flow into a cloud agent context and then out via network egress. The pair lacks an explicit isolation mechanism in the profiles.
conditions: IF business data is written into a Repl workspace file
IF Replit Agent sends workspace contents to external services during task execution
mitigations: Store sensitive exports outside the Repl workspace
Redact business data before handing files to Replit Agent
Limit Replit tasks to synthetic or sample data
Review outbound requests before running long tasks
requires-engineering: enforce workspace-level data loss prevention

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Airbyte has API access and broad egress, while Replit Agent can write the filesystem, modify git state, execute shell, and spawn subprocesses in a persistent Repl filesystem. If both operate on the same repo or workspace, concurrent writes and git mutations can overwrite each other without locking. The profiles show no coordination primitive, so the conflict is materially dangerous.
conditions: IF both agents target the same repository or workspace
IF Airbyte writes generated artifacts while Replit Agent edits the same files or git branch
mitigations: Assign separate directories per agent
Pause one agent before the other edits shared files
Use git branches for each agent's changes
Check for uncommitted diffs before handoff
requires-engineering: add file locks or orchestration locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Airbyte can produce transformed data or pipeline outputs, and Replit Agent can act on files and shell commands inside the workspace. If Replit treats Airbyte output as authoritative without verification, errors can cascade into code changes or deployment steps. The profiles do not show a built-in verification gate, so the default risk is moderate.
conditions: IF Replit Agent consumes Airbyte-generated files as ground truth
IF downstream shell or git actions are triggered from those outputs without review
mitigations: Add a manual verification step before acting on Airbyte output
Compare outputs against source records or checksums
Restrict Replit Agent to read-only review for imported artifacts
Use a checklist for any generated config changes
requires-engineering: add schema validation between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Airbyte touches business data, while Replit Agent handles source code, secrets, and deployment configuration in a cloud Repl. If regulated business data is moved into Replit-managed storage or logs, retention and residency obligations may diverge. The profiles do not document matching compliance controls, so the mismatch is plausible and nontrivial.
conditions: IF regulated business data is transferred into a Replit workspace
IF retention or residency requirements apply to the transferred data class
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in the Repl workspace
Strip secrets before importing files
Confirm retention settings for any uploaded artifacts
Keep compliance-sensitive work in a separate environment
requires-engineering: document a data-handling policy for the pair
